title: SE compliance persona vignettes - WIP
summary: Working set of short, 1-paragraph persona vignettes and micro-battlecards for sales engineers engaging compliance-heavy buyers. Focus is on signal language, demo hooks, legal/infra checklist for pilots, and quick fallback scripts for privacy and data residency objections.
content:
Context: used by SEs during discovery and quick prep before a 30–45min pilot kickoff with compliance or security stakeholders. These are intentionally compact (1-3 bullets per persona) to fit on a tablet or saved in a Notes app.

Notes to self: keep language non-technical for legal contacts; map to logs/audit, key management, data residency early. Add quick diagram later showing control plane vs private deploy boundary.

Persona vignettes (short):

- GRC Gina — Head of Governance, Risk & Compliance (CISO partner): cares about auditability, retention policies, PII handling. Hook: "We separate control plane metadata from customer tokens and provide audit trails for every inference. Typical pilot steps: define retention policy, map PII detectors to sample prompts, and run a 72-hour trace review." Objection script: "If legal asks about data persistence, say: 'By default, hosted inference obfuscates PII, and we can enable ephemeral KV/caching and retention = 0 for pilot datasets.'"

- Platform Paul — Platform/Infra Lead: wants predictable egress, VPC peering, and integration constraints. Hook: "We support VPC connector or private deployment; pilots typically use short-lived dedicated capacity with sample traffic to validate throughput and routing rules." Quick ask list: access policy, IP allowlist, expected QPS, and influence on rate limiting.

- Product-Led Priya — Product manager for user-facing features: cares about latency and quality regressions. Hook: "We can run side-by-side A/B on model variants and measure token economics per route; keep an eval set of 50 representative prompts." Pilot success metrics: p95 latency < target, no more than X% drop in correctness on eval set, cost per thousand tokens below threshold.

- Legal Liaison Leo — Corporate counsel contact: focuses on contract clauses, indemnity, and data processing agreements. Suggested opening: "We have a standard DPA and can add a schedule for data handling that restricts inference logs to SOC2 retention windows; we also can commit to on-prem/private deployments for regulated flows."

Micro-battlecards (one-liners + quick proof points):

- Auditability 
  - Ask: "How are model inferences logged and who can see them?"
  - Script: "All request/response metadata is logged to a tenant-scoped audit trail; logs are exportable to your SIEM and support custom redaction hooks."
  - Proof point: "Customer X ran a 2-week log export to Splunk during a pilot and validated no PII captured in cleartext."

- Data Residency 
  - Ask: "Where will my data be processed and stored?"
  - Script: "Redwood supports region pinning for inference and private deployments for total data locality; hosted defaults to region-specific clusters and we can sign region commitments for enterprise pilots."
  - Proof point: "We have EU-only deployments and two customers in fintech using dedicated pools in eu-west-1."

- Key Management / Encryption 
  - Ask: "How do you handle customer keys?"
  - Script: "Integrates with customer KMS (Cloud KMS/HSM) and supports customer-supplied keys for model artifacts and request-level encryption. Keys never leave your managed key lifecycle unless requested."

Demo hooks and short scripts (30s) for compliance calls:

- "Show audit export": Navigate to Console > Audit > Export; show a sample redaction rule and scheduled export to S3. Call out retention settings.
- "Show private deployment topology": Quick diagram — control plane in Redwood (metadata only) + customer-side inference nodes in VPC; call out no egress unless configured.
- "Simulate PII flow": Use a canned prompt set with redaction turned on; demonstrate request log with redacted fields.

Pilot checklist (for legal/infra + SE):

1) Scope doc: data types, retention windows, success metrics (latency/cost/accuracy)
2) Network: IP allowlist, VPC peering or private endpoint, egress rules
3) Keys & certs: KMS project id, key rotation policy, TLS certs for endpoints
4) Logging & SIEM: where audit logs go, redaction rules, sample export test
5) Compliance docs: DPA, SCCs (if EU), any regulator-specific terms (e.g., HIPAA BAA)
6) Rollback/backout plan: ensure ability to revoke access or route to a lighter-weight hosted variant

Quick fallback language for sensitive objections:

- If "we can't risk user data leaving the environment": "We can run the pilot on private deployment nodes in your VPC — same API surface, full data locality."
- If "we need absolute no-logs": "We offer ephemeral mode for pilot requests: no retained KV cache, retention=0, and audit only at a metadata level if required for compliance sign-off."

Open questions / to-do (short):

- Add example redaction rules with regex snippets for credit-card, SSN, national IDs.
- Build a one-page PDF that legal can sign off quickly: includes DPA summary, pilot scope checklist, and point of contact.
- Create a short recording (2–3 min) demonstrating the Console audit export and region pinning flow for SE enablement library.

Example micro-scripts for SE Slack snippets (copy-paste):

- "Quick note for kickoff: define retention (0/7/30d), designate SIEM target, and confirm KMS project id. If they push back on logs, offer ephemeral mode and private deploy."
- "To legal: attaching DPA + pilot schedule. Please confirm if SCCs required for this scope — happy to have legal sync w/ our counsel (Jordan Blake)."
